research.channel: Zomato (food delivery, India; parent Eternal Ltd) - restaurant partner data availability

data_points.name: Zomato order ID, restaurant/outlet ID (res_id), restaurant name, order placed timestamp
data_points.via: POS order relay (Zomato Order Relay Webhook -> Petpooja)

data_points.name: Order status lifecycle with timestamps (placed, confirmed, ready, rider-assigned, pickedup, delivered, reject, timedout)

data_points.notes: Timestamps are those the POS records when it sends/receives each event. Zomato auto-rejects (timedout) if the outlet does not act within the window (approx 5 min in the guide).

data_points.name: Fulfilment mode: Zomato logistics vs self logistics; delivery vs takeaway
data_points.via: POS order relay / outlet logistics status APIs
data_points.notes: Separate documented flows for Zomato-logistics and self-logistics orders; outlet-level logistics status is readable via API.

data_points.name: Order tags and instructions (cooking instruction, no-cutlery, PURE_VEG, mandatory/skippable item checklist)
data_points.via: POS order relay (order_tags)

data_points.name: Order totals: item subtotal, total charges, total taxes, total discount, customer payable
data_points.via: POS order relay
data_points.notes: Field-level names for Zomato are gated; UrbanPiper's normalised relay exposes order_subtotal, total_taxes, total_charges, total_external_discount, order_total, payable_amount.

data_points.name: Order history / sales report export from partner dashboard
data_points.via: partner dashboard export (Reporting > business reports)
data_points.granularity: per order / per day (exact columns unverified)
data_points.notes: A reporting section exists at zomato.com/partners/onlineordering/reporting (login required). I could not verify the export column list; rely on POS data + settlement report for order-level mock data.

data_points.name: Item-level name, quantity, unit price, variants and add-ons
data_points.via: POS order relay
data_points.notes: Zomato's critical feature list requires POS to show item name, description and add-ons selected; variants have separate prices.

data_points.name: Item-level taxes, charges and item-level discount

data_points.notes: UrbanPiper confirms order-level and item-level discount, charge and tax info is relayed for Zomato.

data_points.via: partner dashboard / partner app (aggregate insight only)

data_points.name: Dish-level ratings
data_points.via: partner dashboard (unverified)

data_points.name: Packaging charge (restaurant-set, fixed PC_D_F or percentage PC_D_P)

access_routes.route: POS order relay via Zomato POS Integration API (Zomato -> Petpooja)
access_routes.what_it_gives: Real-time order header, items, variants/add-ons, packaging charge, taxes, discounts by category (restaurant vs Zomato funded), payment mode, KPT, order tags, status events, rider status events, MAC cancellation requests, complaints relay, per-order ratings (API + webhook), masked contact on demand, item stock toggles, outlet on/off and timings, menu sync/moderation status. No fees, commission, payout, funnel or ads data.
access_routes.prerequisites: Each outlet's Zomato res_id mapped in Petpooja with Zomato integration enabled. The field-level API reference is login-gated to integration partners (organisation email); what the ERP actually receives is whatever Petpooja stores and exposes from the relay.

access_routes.what_it_gives: Business reports (delivered orders, sales, AOV, bad orders, customer funnel, marketing, dish trends), ads campaign setup and performance, offers, customer issues/complaints, reviews, payouts and statement of account, multi-outlet switching.

access_routes.prerequisites: Correct PAN and GSTIN registered with Zomato per legal entity.

research.settlement_mechanics:
Cycle: Zomato T&C clause 9 - orders serviced Monday to Sunday are settled on or before Thursday of the following week (next working day if a bank holiday), i.e. a 4 to 10 day lag from order date; secondary sources report 10-14 days in stressed periods. Options: settlement within 3 bank working days if opted in the enrolment form; 'daily payouts' (launched Jan 2024, no extra cost, based on sales from three days prior) only for outlets with 100 or fewer orders a month - not applicable to a busy QSR outlet. One net bank credit per outlet per cycle, traceable by UTR in the settlement report.

Deductions per T&C: (a) service fee (commission) on both COD and online orders, (b) payment mechanism fee, (c) tax collected by Zomato on restaurant service, (d) any other amounts due with consent (ads, Hyperpure, Gold/brand packs, etc.). Zomato may also set off dues to any group company. The settlement workbook shows, per order: subtotal, packaging charge, delivery charge, restaurant discount [Promo], restaurant discount [flat offs, freebies, Gold and others], total GST collected from customers, service fee % and amount, payment mechanism fee, logistics charge, taxes (18% GST) on service and payment mechanism fees, applicable amount for 9(5), GST paid by Zomato on behalf of restaurant under s.9(5), applicable amount for TCS, TCS, TDS 194O amount, customer compensation/recoupment, other order-level deductions (cash received on self-delivery orders, credit/debit note adjustment, promo recovery adjustment, extra inventory ads), net additions, net deductions, order-level payout, settlement status/date, bank UTR, unsettled amount. A separate 'Addition Deductions Details' tab lists additions (e.g. cancellation compensation) and deductions A) growth services incl. ADS, B) Hyperpure, C) other, D) adjustments from previous weeks, with 'Total amount' vs 'Adjusted amount' (what actually left this payout).

GST s.9(5): since 1 Jan 2022 Zomato is the deemed supplier for restaurant service; it charges 5% GST to the customer, collects it and deposits it itself. In the payout the GST is shown as collected and then fully deducted ('GST paid by Zomato on behalf of restaurant'), so restaurant revenue from Zomato should be modelled net of GST and no output GST liability arises for the outlet on these orders (they are still reported in GSTR-1/3B as ECO supplies). TCS u/s 52 is not collected on 9(5) restaurant services (CBIC Circular 167/23/2021); it applies only to any non-restaurant-service supplies, at 0.5% since 10 Jul 2024.

TDS: deducted by Zomato on gross sales less taxes, 0.1% since 1 Oct 2024 (s.194-O; re-codified as s.393(1) of the Income-tax Act 2025 from 1 Apr 2026, which Zomato's T&C now cite). Appears per order in the settlement report; quarterly TDS certificate; creditable via Form 26AS. Separately, the restaurant may have to deduct TDS on Zomato's service fee/ads and claim reimbursement from Zomato against a certificate.

Ads: Zomato ad terms state spends are recovered by reduction from weekly payouts and shown separately on the statement of account, with a monthly invoice. Refunds/complaints: amounts refunded to customers for restaurant-attributable issues are recouped from payouts (Problem Order clause); a mandatory 50:50 refund share was paused in May 2025. Cancellations not attributable to the restaurant are compensated at 100% / 80% / 40% per the compensation policy and appear as additions. Monthly tax invoice for all fees is issued within 7 days of month end.

typical_rates.value: Reported range 10-28% (Sept 2025); typical 25-27% for single outlets, 18-22% negotiated for chains with scale (2026 blog); another CA source quotes 18-35%. Set in each restaurant's enrolment form - not public. A 5-outlet Mumbai QSR chain at roughly 20-24% is a defensible mock assumption.

0.5% (0.25% CGST + 0.25% SGST) since 10 Jul 2024; not applicable to restaurant services under s.9(5)

typical_rates.value: Weekly: Mon-Sun orders paid on or before Thursday of the following week. Daily payout option only for outlets with 100 or fewer orders per month (sales from three days prior). 3-bank-working-day option if chosen in the form.

100% of a successful order if cancelled after rider pickup; 80% of net order value if marked ready accurately and weekly FOR accuracy is 80% or more; otherwise 40%; nil if cancelled within 60 seconds or if restaurant-attributable

caveats: Zomato's field-level API reference (api-reference/v1/endpoints and /webhooks) is login-gated ('Please login with your organization email ID first'). I did not bypass it. Relay field claims rest on Zomato's public guide/glossary pages plus UrbanPiper's normalised payload docs, so exact Zomato field names are not verified.

What the ERP can actually use from the relay depends on what Petpooja persists and exposes (e.g. whether it stores the Zomato discount category PROMO vs ZOMATO_VOUCHER/PEPPER). Confirm with Petpooja before promising a restaurant-vs-platform discount split.

Commission and payment mechanism fee ARE visible per order, but only in the weekly settlement report after the cycle closes - not with the live order and not via API. In the mock, show actual fees only for settled weeks and label current-week fees as estimates from the contracted rate.

Scribd copies of real Zomato settlement reports could not be fetched (connection refused); column names quoted come from search-result snippets of those documents and from a DEV Community analysis of real payout files. Treat exact column labels as medium confidence.

The DEV analysis found that Zomato's settlement workbook does not state who funded each discount and that its 'Offers and Discounts Summary' tab is broken; the restaurant-funded amounts do appear as 'Restaurant discount' columns. The platform-funded portion is therefore only inferable from the POS relay categories.

Customer PII: default is masked. Phone sharing is an opt-in pilot announced Nov 2025 (phone number only, consent irrevocable); I could not verify its rollout status as of Sept 2026. Zomato T&C prohibit using Customer Data for marketing, list enhancement or feedback. Safest for the mock: no Zomato customer names/phones, no customer-level cohorts or LTV; at most aggregate new/repeat percentages labelled as dashboard-sourced.

Partner-dashboard metrics (funnel, customer mix, ads impressions/clicks/ROI, dish trends, bad orders) are supported only by app-store descriptions and secondary marketing blogs; exact metric names, granularity and export options are unverified. Present them as outlet-level weekly aggregates entered/imported from the dashboard, never as order-level or API data.

TDS section reference changed: Zomato's current T&C cite s.393(1) of the Income-tax Act 2025 (effective 1 Apr 2026) instead of s.194-O; settlement report labels seen in 2025 files still read 'TDS 194O'. Suggest labelling 'TDS u/s 393(1) (formerly 194-O)' at 0.1%. Several 2026 blogs still quote the obsolete 1% rate.
TCS should be zero or negligible for a kebab/biryani QSR because 9(5) restaurant services are excluded from TCS; do not model a 1% TCS deduction as some blogs suggest.
Commission rates are contractual and confidential; all percentages are reported ranges. The payment mechanism fee figure (1.84%) comes from an older enrolment form snippet.

The 50:50 mandatory refund cost-sharing scheme was paused in May 2025 with a stated intent to relaunch; current status not verified. Penalty line items for rejections/timeouts are permitted by T&C but their exact appearance in reports is unverified.

Per-order delivery distance, payment instrument (UPI/card), customer-side platform/COD fees, rider payout and a persistent customer ID were not found in any source; treat as not available in the mock.
Zomato introduced a customer-side 'Pay on Delivery' fee in Sept 2026; this is charged to customers, not a restaurant deduction, and should not appear in outlet economics.

UrbanPiper's old Helpjuice knowledge base (source of the 'phone and email are masked; last 4 digits of relayed phone are the Zomato rider OTP' statement) is now offline; that detail survives only in search snippets.

rate_corrections: Payment mechanism fee: upgrade from 'low confidence, older form' to medium-high. 1.84% of order value is corroborated by CNBC-TV18 (Feb 2023), enrolment forms dated 2020 and Mar 2024, a Sept 2026 CAclubindia worked example and a 2026 onboarding reel ('Base service fee 25%, 1.84% payment mechanism fee'). Use 1.84% in the mock; drop the 1.8-2.5% range. Note older forms say it applies to online-paid orders only. https://www.cnbctv18.com/business/ (search: 'payment mechanism fee 1.84 percent')

Ads 'typically 4-9% of aggregator revenue': NOT supported by the cited digitalcatapult guide (it gives CPC Rs 4-18, starter budget Rs 15,000-40,000/outlet/month, CPO Rs 40-65 for QSR/biryani, ROAS 4x-5x for QSR, but no percent-of-revenue figure). Remove the 4-9% claim or mark it as our own assumption. https://digitalcatapult.in/blog/zomato-ads-complete-guide-2026

Ad pricing unit: Zomato contracts on CPV (cost per visit), not CPC. Secondary sources quote Rs 5-15 per click (Restaurant India, May 2026) and Rs 4-18 (digitalcatapult). Label as 'cost per visit' in the mock. https://www.restaurantindia.in/article/zomato-ads-cost-is-restaurant-advertising-worth-it.16009

Service fee: 10-28% reported range confirmed (Verdict Foodservice, 1 Sep 2025). New-outlet base service fee of 25% seen in 2026 onboarding material. 20-24% for a 5-outlet chain remains a reasonable assumption, but it must be labelled 'assumed contract rate'. Total service fee incl. long-distance fee capped at 30% (Medianama) and the cap shows as its own discount line in the settlement report. https://www.verdictfoodservice.com/news/eternal-explores-changes-zomato/

Long-distance fee bands confirmed: Rs 20 (4-6 km, order > Rs 150), Rs 40 (> 6 km); additionally Rs 40 applies to orders under Rs 150 beyond 6 km, and no fee under Rs 150 within 6 km. https://www.medianama.com/2025/07/223-zomato-long-distance-delivery-fee-restaurants/

TDS: 0.1% confirmed (dineomai Sep 2026, hellobooks Jul 2026); T&C text verified to cite s.393(1) ITA 2025 on 'Gross Sales (less applicable taxes charged by the Restaurant)'. Settlement line label in real files is 'TDS 194O amount'. Terra-insight (1% TDS, 1% TCS) and menuhelper (1% TDS) are wrong/outdated - do not use them for rates. https://www.zomato.com/policies/online-ordering/
TCS: line label in real files is 'Tax collected at source + TCS IGST amount' and is Rs 0.00 in every restaurant report snippet seen - model as zero. https://dineomai.com/blog/zomato-payout-deductions

Payout cycle verified verbatim in T&C: Mon-Sun orders paid 'on or before Thursday of the following week'; 3-bank-working-day option if chosen in the Form; daily payouts only for outlets with 100 or fewer orders a month (Zomato blog, Jan 2024). menuhelper's '7-business-day' / '10-14 days' is anecdotal - do not use as the norm.

Net realisation: terra-insight's '~65% of gross' is from an article that gets TDS/TCS wrong; treat 62-70% as indicative only and let the mock's own arithmetic (commission + 1.84% + 18% GST on fees + 0.1% TDS + restaurant-funded discounts + ads) produce the figure.

Cancellation compensation verified verbatim: 100% after pickup; 80% of Net Order Value if marked ready accurately and previous-week accuracy >= 80%; else 40%; nil within 60 seconds or if restaurant-attributable; self-logistics: 100% if cancelled after 80% of estimated delivery time, else 40%. https://www.zomato.com/o2termscompensationpolicy/india
Customer-side Pay-on-Delivery fee confirmed (from about 11 Sep 2026; Rs 5 upward, reported up to 2% capped at Rs 30). Customer-side only; keep out of outlet economics.

verify.notes:
The WebSearch budget was exhausted, so searches went through the browser pane (Google and Bing). Primary Zomato pages were read directly. Scribd is blocked in both the browser and WebFetch, so the settlement-report column evidence comes from Google snippets of about ten real reports dated Jul 2024 to Oct 2025. The labels agree across those files, but the evidence is second-hand, so treat it as medium confidence.

**Verified directly on Zomato's own pages**
- The discount category glossary.
- The charges, KPT and rejection-reason glossaries.
- The order-management endpoints, including the ratings, complaints, MAC and masked contact-details endpoints.
- The critical feature list.
- The Zomato-logistics rider statuses.
- The field-level API reference is login-gated, so exact relay field names remain unverified. I did not try to get past the login.
- The T&C clauses checked:
  - Settlement cycle: Monday to Sunday, paid by Thursday.
  - Deductions.
  - TDS under s.393(1).
  - Monthly invoice within 7 days.
  - Customer Data restrictions in clause 14.
  - Additional charges for rejections.
- The compensation policy, the daily payouts blog, and the ad terms (Total CV, weekly statement of account, payout deduction, Visit and CPV definitions).

**Headline verdicts**
- **Commission per order:** It is visible per order, but only in the weekly settlement report after the cycle closes. It is never in the relay and never available through an API.
  - The UrbanPiper payload confirms there is no fee field.
  - Petpooja's own reconciliation product requires the restaurant to share its payout reports.
  - The fee structure is richer than the researcher described. It has a commissionable value, a base fee, a distance or fulfilment fee, a 30% cap discount and a payment mechanism fee.
- **Customer PII:** The researcher's conservative stance holds.
  - Only masked contact on demand is available.
  - The phone opt-in is a Nov 2025 early-stage feature, and I found no 2026 rollout evidence.
  - UrbanPiper says aggregator customer data "might be dummy".
  - One new finding: the settlement file has a "Customer ID" column whose nature is unknown. It stays out of the mock.
- **Discount funding split:** The restaurant-funded portion is firm. The Zomato-funded portion comes only from relay categories and depends on what Petpooja stores. The settlement file never states Zomato's share.
- **Funnel and ads:** These are real dashboard aggregates, corroborated by practitioners. There is no API. One large QSR had to scrape the dashboard to get them. The researcher's app-store citations for "customer funnel", "dish trends" and "bad orders" do not match the current listings.
- **Payout columns:** Broadly corroborated and extended with distance and fulfilment-fee columns, penalty lines and the Discount Construct column.

**Source reliability**
- terra-insight and menuhelper quote obsolete 1% TDS and TCS rates. Do not use either for rates.
- The dev.to analysis is a two-day-old single-author post. It is consistent with the other evidence but unaudited.
- The digitalcatapult and chuk.in posts are marketing blogs with no screenshots.

No files were written.
